thread:
Maya: Quick sync — building the operator inbox for automatic degrade/fallback. Goal: let humans intervene without creating alert noise. What does 'minimal' look like?

Devon: Minimal IMO: a single compact inbox card with 3 lines: reason, affected route, 1-click actions. Actions = Acknowledge, Snooze (10m/1h), Force-fallback. Keep trace links off by default.

Alex: Add audit metadata to every action: actor, policy_id, route, reason, policy_version. Must be immutable and queryable.

Tara: UX sketch: card header = "Degrade triggered", small badge for signal (error, latency, quota). Tapping expands to show last 3 traces and a short timeline. Buttons below.

Jordan: Concern: operator-induced flapping. If they force-fallback rapidly we'll hide underlying issues. We need guardrails — soft limits on force-actions + automatic cooldown.

Devon: Proposed guardrail: allow one manual force-per-route per 30m; extra forces require Escalate permission or an explicit confirmation modal explaining risk.

Maya: Also want a lightweight "preview" mode: roll the fallback to a 1% shadow sample so operator sees effect without impacting production. It should be labelled clearly as simulated.

Alex: Good. Simulation must still emit an audit entry with simulated=true. That way we can trace experiments.

sre-bot: deploy-notice: feature/operator-inbox toggled to staging (commit 3a7b9c).

Tara: RBAC: default role "observer" gets Acknowledge/Snooze only. "Operator" can Force-fallback but within rate-limits. "Admin" can override rate-limits. We'll add this mapping to the RBAC policy page.

Jordan: Telemetry: when an operator acts, capture a snapshot of p50/p95 latency, error-rate, and throughput for 5m before and 10m after action. Attach to audit id.

Devon: Implementation note: we should sample traces (last 3) and a compact signal sparkline in the card. Expand shows the histogram and the exact threshold that fired (e.g., "error_rate 8.3% > threshold 5% over 2m").

Maya: Can we make "Snooze" only suppress inbox noise for that operator/team? Don't silence the actual degrade or metrics — we need alerts to continue for ops.

Alex: Yep — snooze should be just UI-level suppression and an audit event. Force-fallback is the only action that modifies routing state.

Devon: Proposed internal API endpoint stub:
```
POST /internal/operator-action
{ actor, action, route, policy_id, reason, simulated }
// response: { audit_id }
```
Make action values enum: acknowledge, snooze, force_fallback, preview_simulation, escalate.

Tara: Audit retention: keep 90 days default; enterprise can request longer retention or export. Exports should include telemetry snapshot links and trace IDs.

Jordan: For oscillation detection, add a watch that flags routes with >3 manual force actions in 24h and surfaces to SRE for review.

Maya: Onboarding checklist (in-console modal): 1) What fired (signal + threshold) 2) What fallback is used and expected user impact 3) How to escalate and who to @. Keep to 3 bullets.

Alex: UI copy suggestion for the card header: "Automatic fallback triggered — action recommended" and small help icon linking to the checklist.

Devon: I'll wire up the rate-limit checks on the backend and the telemetry snapshot logic. Add audit immutability via append-only store.

Tara: I'll add RBAC matrix and small copy for the onboarding modal. Also add a checkbox for "I confirm forced fallback" when rate-limit is exceeded.

Jordan: I'll build the 1% preview sandbox. Important: simulated requests must not touch production logging paths (use sandbox logging) but still surface simulated telemetry to the audit.

Maya: Excellent. Action items: Alex -> wireframe + API contract; Devon -> rate-limits + telemetry hooks; Jordan -> preview sandbox; Tara -> RBAC + onboarding copy. We'll reconvene tomorrow for review. :thumbsup:
